record.name: Tennessee Driver Services Multi-Channel AI
record.organisation: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security
record.description: Tennessee's Department of Safety and Homeland Security deployed AI-powered tools across chat (December 2025), email (February 2026), and voice channels to handle public enquiries about driver services. The system uses the agency's website as a single source of truth to answer questions autonomously, handling approximately 1,000 daily chat interactions with a 70% resolution rate and operating 24/7 to bridge the gap between high demand (3,000-5,000 daily contacts) and limited staff capacity (1,000).
record.novelty: Using the public website as the sole data source creates a feedback loop where AI errors reveal website inaccuracies, enabling rapid iterative content correction. The system can be reconfigured within minutes to address emerging situations like weather-related closures or scam alerts without traditional technical deployment delays.
record.stakeholders: Tennessee citizens seeking driver services information, TDOS customer service staff who handle the 20% of escalated queries, and TDOS management benefiting from 24/7 automated coverage.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously answers 70% of queries, deflects 10% of non-genuine messages, and escalates 20% to humans without requiring human initiation per interaction. When configured with new use cases—such as identifying scam text enquiries or providing county-specific closure status during an ice storm—it autonomously handles these scenarios 'within minutes of the need being identified,' whereas previously a human agent would have needed to look up that information.
record.tech_details: Built on Zendesk's agentic AI platform with a retrieval architecture drawing exclusively from the agency's public website as the single source of truth. Deployed across three channels—chat (live), email (live), and voice (in final testing)—with text-back capabilities for voice to share links post-call.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Tennessee: AI-powered customer service across chat, email, and voice

record.name: JnA AI Bot
record.description: A WhatsApp-based AI assistant that automatically scans community health data from the Jamii ni Afya platform at month-end, identifies priority trends such as rising disease cases, and generates ready-to-use supervision agendas with talking points and anticipated questions for community health worker meetings. Piloted across two districts in Zanzibar with supervisors and community health workers.
record.novelty: Brings automated data synthesis and agenda generation directly into supervisors' existing WhatsApp workflows rather than requiring new apps or dashboards; co-designed with frontline supervisors to ensure insights support collaborative problem-solving rather than performance review.
record.stakeholders: Community health supervisors, community health workers (CHWs), Ministry of Health, D-tree, Dalberg Data Insights, Dalberg Design; ultimately households receiving targeted health education.
record.agentic_rationale: The bot autonomously scans recent data in a supervisor's catchment area near month-end, selects priority topics to flag (e.g., 'Rising child fever cases'), generates complete coaching agendas including learning objectives and talking points, and responds to follow-up questions in plain language without human initiation of each step.
record.tech_details: WhatsApp-based interface; uses JnA platform data; generates trend briefs and conversational responses grounded in Ministry of Health guidance; designed to operate on community-level aggregated data with guardrails excluding individual patient records and clinical diagnoses.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Zanzibar: Jamii ni Afya AI bot

record.name: CHA AI Assistant
record.description: A WhatsApp-based AI tool that translates raw data from Kenya's Electronic Community Health Information System (eCHIS) into timely performance nudges and emerging health trend alerts for Community Health Assistants (CHAs). The assistant automates the synthesis of routine community health data to help CHAs prepare for supervision meetings, identify priorities, and coach Community Health Promoters more effectively.
record.novelty: The tool operates within existing CHA workflows via WhatsApp rather than requiring a new app, and it closes the loop by returning aggregated data insights back to frontline supervisors rather than only flowing upward to national reporting systems.
record.stakeholders: Community Health Assistants (supervisors), Community Health Promoters (frontline workers), Ministry of Health, Amref Health Africa, Dalberg Data Insights, and Dalberg Design.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI assistant autonomously analyzes raw eCHIS data to "summarize patterns, surface trends, and highlight potential issues" without CHAs manually reviewing each CHP's data, delivering "timely performance nudges and emerging health trend alerts" at month-end to identify priorities for upcoming meetings. CHAs previously had to manually check each CHP's data as it came in; the system now proactively generates insights that 88% of CHAs received and 83% used to guide meetings.
record.tech_details: WhatsApp-based interface; processes aggregated data from Kenya's Electronic Community Health Information System (eCHIS); designed to mirror existing CHA workflow rhythms with end-of-month trend alerts.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Kenya: AI supervision assistant for community health

record.name: Automated Aviation Safety Issue Analysis App
record.organisation: Aviation Safety Technology Institute (Republic of Korea), with National Information Society Agency
record.description: An AI-powered application that automates the processing and analysis of aviation safety data. Users input accident-related documents, and the system automatically translates, summarizes, classifies the accident type, and provides associated risk factors. The app also generates Excel files for secondary analysis and retrieves similar historical accident cases. It was developed to address inefficiencies in manual data processing by specialized analysts and support compliance with ICAO international standards for national aviation safety management.
record.novelty: The system represents a shift from manual data integration and analysis by specialized analysts to automated, end-to-end processing of unstructured aviation accident documents using generative AI. It combines document ingestion, multilingual translation, summarization, classification, and risk factor extraction in a single automated workflow.
record.stakeholders: Safety managers and data analysts at airlines, airports, national aviation agencies, and the Aviation Safety Technology Institute; ultimately the flying public who benefit from improved safety.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously executes a multi-step analytical workflow upon document input: it 'automatically classifies the accident type' and 'provides associated risk factors' without human initiation of each step. The source states that inputting documents 'triggers translation and summarization' and that the app was developed to validate 'automation performance' for 'AI-based aviation safety data processing, safety issue identification, and document generation'.
record.tech_details: Built using a large language model (LLM) fine-tuned on Q&A datasets derived from SKYbrary aviation accident articles, with an established aviation accident classification system and risk factor database. The system preprocesses data into LLM-understandable format and was optimized through continuous technical review.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Automated Analysis of Aviation Safety Issues: Hyper-Scale AI PoC

record.name: Fire Access Route and Evacuation Route Guidance System
record.organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
record.description: An AI and IoT-integrated system that analyzes real-time building data to calculate optimal evacuation routes for occupants and access routes for firefighters during fire incidents. It extends beyond traditional alarm notifications to provide dynamic, data-driven guidance for emergency response. Launched in 2024.
record.novelty: Moves beyond static alarm systems to real-time, adaptive route optimization that simultaneously serves both evacuees and emergency responders using live sensor data.
record.stakeholders: Building occupants, firefighters, fire safety managers, and the National Information Society Agency as implementing body.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously analyzes real-time information and provides optimal routes without requiring human initiation of each calculation; it independently determines and delivers evacuation and access strategies based on live data analysis during active fire incidents.
record.tech_details: Integrates AI with IoT sensors for real-time data collection and processing; specific models or platforms not stated.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Development of a Fire Access Route and Evacuation Route Guidance System based on the BDApp (Fire Remote Control Service)

record.name: AI Prediction and Control Solution for Fine Dust Reduction
record.description: An AI and IoT-enabled system deployed in multi-use public facilities (subway stations, airports, shopping malls, hospitals) that predicts real-time changes in fine dust concentrations and automatically regulates indoor air quality. It replaces traditional periodic filter replacement and manual ventilation adjustments with automated detection and optimal air quality maintenance measures to protect user health.
record.novelty: Moves beyond reactive, manual facility management to predictive, autonomous control of indoor air quality by integrating AI prediction with IoT sensor networks for real-time environmental regulation.
record.stakeholders: Users of multi-use public facilities, facility management operators, and the National Information Society Agency.
record.agentic_rationale: The system detects fine dust concentrations in real time and automatically executes optimal air quality maintenance measures without requiring human initiation for each ventilation adjustment or control action.
record.tech_details: Combines AI prediction models with IoT sensor networks for real-time fine dust monitoring and automated control of ventilation and air filtration systems.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Development of AI Prediction and Control Solution for Fine Dust Reduction in Multi-Use

record.name: Yukti
record.description: Yukti is a bilingual voice AI mentor designed to help engineering students build AI and machine learning projects for their portfolios. Operating in Tamil and English through a Telegram bot, it conducts Socratic mentoring conversations via voice calls to guide students through problem-solving rather than providing direct answers. The pilot currently serves over 1,100 students in Tamil Nadu's state skills programme.
record.novelty: The system employs a Socratic questioning approach where the AI asks follow-up questions rather than giving answers, designed specifically to prevent students from bypassing learning. It features proactive outreach capabilities, autonomously contacting disengaged students to understand barriers, and operates bilingually to bridge language gaps in technical education.
record.stakeholders: Engineering students across Tamil Nadu, particularly those outside metropolitan centres with limited mentorship access; Tamil Nadu Skill Development Corporation; Sustainable Living Lab India (implementer).
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously reaches out to students who had not been engaging to understand barriers they face, and conducts mentoring conversations using Socratic dialogue—asking follow-up questions and guiding students toward working through problems themselves without a human initiating each exchange. After conversations, it autonomously shares action items with students.
record.tech_details: Speech-to-speech architecture using Google Gemini as the underlying model, with an added context layer specific to course content and mentorship processes. Deployed as a Telegram bot that initiates voice callbacks to students' phones and supports multiple personas for different mentoring stages (e.g., presentation coaching, technical questions).

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Yukti: Conversational AI voice agent mentorship platform

record.name: Youth Policy Customized Platform
record.organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
record.description: The platform automatically aggregates and categorizes fragmented youth policy data from central ministries, local governments and public institutions nationwide. It uses AI to deliver personalized policy recommendations to young people and enables direct in-platform applications via Direct Link Policy (DLP) technology, complemented by real-time notifications for key benefits.
record.novelty: It consolidates previously siloed government policy information into a unified, proactive service that automates the entire journey from discovery to application, mirroring the user experience of popular private-sector platforms.
record.stakeholders: Young citizens seeking benefits, parents and caregivers (including those in Seoul’s Borderline Intelligence Program), and public officials using accumulated data to identify children requiring targeted educational support.
record.agentic_rationale: The system autonomously executes multi-step workflows: it automatically collects and categorizes nationwide policy data without manual curation, determines eligibility and recommends personalized policies via AI, and initiates applications through DLP (Direct Link Policy) technology while dispatching real-time notifications, constituting an "automated application system" that does not require human initiation for each step.
record.tech_details: Employs AI for personalized recommendations, DLP (Direct Link Policy) technology for integrated application submission, and continuous data learning to improve accuracy; aggregates data from central and local government sources through interfaces modeled on private platforms popular with youth.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: AI-Based Customized Youth Policy Recommendations and Notifications

record.name: Legi-Assist
record.description: An open-source tool that automatically ingests and analyzes new Maryland state legislation nightly using large language models. It converts bill PDFs to machine-readable text, programmatically detects and excludes struck-through (repealed) text to analyze only current law, compares bill content against agency profiles to determine relevance, and delivers personalized, ranked shortlists of relevant bills to over 120 state agencies each morning.
record.novelty: Purpose-built capability to interpret legal formatting (strikethrough text denoting repealed law) that general AI tools typically misread as active text, combined with a relevance engine that matches bills against detailed agency profiles to surface substantive connections missed by keyword searches.
record.stakeholders: Over 120 Maryland state agencies and teams receiving daily tailored bill rankings, legislative staff, the Innovation Team's data scientists, and other state governments adopting the open-source code.
record.agentic_rationale: The system runs autonomously overnight during legislative sessions to pull new bills from the General Assembly feed, process PDFs, analyze content using LLMs against agency profiles to determine relevance and affected parties, and generate/distribute ranked shortlists to over 120 agencies without a human initiating analysis for each individual bill. It concretely decides which bills affect which agencies and explains the relevance reasoning.
record.tech_details: Built internally using large language models for natural language processing and relevance matching, with custom programming to detect strikethrough formatting in legislative PDFs. The system integrates with the Maryland General Assembly's bill feed and maintains a database of agency profiles for the relevance engine.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Legi-Assist: How Maryland built an open-source tool to track and analyse legislation using AI

record.name: AI-powered Initial Counseling for Welfare Blind Spots
record.organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
record.description: An AI system that analyzes big data on utility disconnections and welfare crisis app reports to proactively identify at-risk households, then initiates automated phone calls to assess welfare needs across health, economic, employment, housing and safety domains. The service transmits consultation results to local government officials who provide in-depth counseling and support. Launched nationwide across 229 local governments in November 2024 after pilots, it served 220,000 people in 2024 with plans to reach 500,000 annually.
record.novelty: Proactively identifies welfare blind spots through real-time big data surveillance of utility disconnections combined with autonomous AI outreach, replacing passive application-based systems with predictive intervention.
record.stakeholders: Vulnerable households facing utility disconnections, local government welfare departments, and the National Information Society Agency.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI autonomously initiates initial consultation calls to individuals identified via big data analysis and, during the conversation, assesses 'the nature of the crisis and welfare needs—such as health, economic, employment, housing, and safety' before transmitting results to officials without human initiation of each contact.
record.tech_details: Utilizes big data analysis of utility disconnection records (electricity, water, gas), AI-powered voice consultation technology, SMS notification gateways, and integration with the welfare crisis alert app and local government case management systems.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Eliminating Welfare Blind Spots through AI-Powered Initial Counseling

record.name: Shucle AI-powered on-demand transport
record.description: A pilot project in Gödöllő, Hungary testing Shucle, an AI-powered demand-responsive transport platform developed by Hyundai Motor Company. Two vehicles replaced fixed-route buses for 11 weeks, dynamically calculating optimal pickup and dropoff routes in real time based on passenger requests. Wait times fell from 60 to 6 minutes with 2,950 residents using the service.
record.novelty: First deployment of Hyundai's Shucle platform outside South Korea, representing a shift from fixed-schedule public transport to fully dynamic, AI-routed on-demand service in a small European city.
record.stakeholders: Residents of Gödöllő needing public transport, municipality transport planners, local bus operators, Hyundai Motor Company, and the Korean-Hungarian Economic Innovation Partnership Program.
record.agentic_rationale: The AI "calculates the most efficient route to pick up and drop off multiple passengers, adjusting continuously as new requests come in" and "only dispatches vehicles in response to actual ride requests" without human intervention for each routing decision. Vehicles autonomously determine where to go based on real-time demand rather than following predetermined routes or schedules.
record.tech_details: Hyundai's Shucle platform using AI algorithms for real-time route optimization; passenger-facing mobile app for ride requests; integration with existing municipal bus network infrastructure.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Shucle: AI-powered on-demand public transport tested in Hungary

record.name: Diia.AI
record.description: Diia.AI is an AI assistant integrated into Ukraine's Diia platform that allows citizens to complete government services through natural language chat conversations. Rather than navigating portals and forms, users describe their needs in plain language, and the assistant connects to live government databases to retrieve information and complete transactions such as income certificates entirely within the chat. The system aims to reduce administrative burden, with projected savings of over one million citizen-hours annually and a 30% reduction in staff-handled enquiries.
record.novelty: Recognized by the World Record Book as the world's first national AI assistant for government services, it employs a privacy-by-design architecture where all identifying information is replaced with neutral placeholders before reaching the AI model, ensuring sensitive personal data never leaves government-controlled infrastructure while still leveraging commercial language models.
record.stakeholders: Citizens accessing government services (particularly older or less digitally confident users), Ministry of Digital Transformation staff, technology partners Google and KitSoft, and ElevenLabs for voice capabilities.
record.agentic_rationale: The assistant connects to relevant government databases, retrieves the citizen's information, and completes the process within the conversation without requiring users to locate or fill forms manually. Unlike conventional chatbots, it "can complete transactions on the citizen's behalf," such as generating income certificates by autonomously executing the service workflow from natural language requests.
record.tech_details: Built on Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash combined with Ukraine's secure government systems and Diia.Engine national digital infrastructure. Uses a four-stage anonymization process where identifying data is swapped for placeholders before AI processing, with responses matched back to citizens via a secure government layer.

source_titles.https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-: Diia.AI: Ukraine's national AI assistant for government services
